component_findings.abstraction_ceremony: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Reusable abstractions such as types, interfaces/traits/generics or equivalent mechanisms can be declared and consumed without excessive scaffolding. Evidence basis: TypeScript | Static source inspection of assigned readable programs (template/programs/typescript/micro and adversarial) under frozen workload definitions. No execution/runtime timing performed by this worker; conciseness scored from source-level expressiveness per unit of semantic work, following language_quality.md fairness rules (idiomatic, non-degraded code; no algorithm substitution). | MB03 (integer arithmetic mix) implemented in 61 lines including required boilerplate (declare const process/require shims needed because the frozen build compiles a single .ts file without @types/node). The core workload() function is 16 lines and directly expresses the five pinned arithmetic operations with no extra scaffolding. | TypeScript's structural typing, arrow functions, template literals, and interface destructuring keep per-operation code compact; modular reduction and floor-division expressed as single-line arithmetic without explicit casts since values stay within the safe integer range (< 2^53). | Ambient declarations for process/require (~10 lines) are an artifact of the frozen no-@types/node build recipe, not a language conciseness deficiency; identical overhead appears across all TS micro-benchmarks reviewed (mb00-mb11). | Adversarial corpus (ADV-01..26) is terse and idiomatic: most single-concept adversarial cases are under 20 lines (e.g. ADV-02_C.ts at 137 bytes), consist…

metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.selection_rule: Judge intrinsic mandatory ceremony for the same kinds of ordinary programs. Do not reuse raw LOC/bytes/tokens as the score and do not reward external libraries.

component_findings.consistency_regular_forms: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Similar concepts use regular forms with few special-case spellings or context-dependent surface rules. Evidence basis: TypeScript | Static source inspection of the same corpus; readability scored on naming clarity, structural decomposition, comment/documentation practice, and syntactic clarity of control flow, per language_quality.md guidance to use idiomatic, production-reasonable style. | Workload files (mb00-mb11) carry frozen-spec header comments citing the exact methodology section and pinned constants, plus explanatory comments for non-obvious representability/precision reasoning (e.g. mb03.ts explains why plain number is exact and why 32-bit XOR semantics hold) -- exemplary self-documenting style enabled by TS comment conventions. | Function decomposition is clean: workload() isolates pure computation from main()'s I/O/mode-handling concerns, aided by TypeScript interfaces (Mb03Result) giving named, self-describing return shapes instead of anonymous tuples/arrays -- a readability advantage over languages lacking structural return types. | Control flow is linear and idiomatic (for-loops, no clever bit tricks substituted for pinned arithmetic), matching the requirement that no algorithmic optimizations obscure the reference computation. | Naming is consistent and descriptive (sAdd, sXor, sMul, sDiv mirror the spec's operation names) across all reviewed micro-benchmarks, aiding cross-file comparison. | Minor readability friction: ambient declare blocks and require/hrtime typings needed for…
